root: ^The checkpoint queue barely moves. A bored guard waves cars through two at a time, more interested in his handheld than your badge.

b: ^The Hustle reads the guard's boredom as an opening — a story here could shave ten minutes off the wait.
^You settle in for the wait like everyone else.

root: ^A mask-seal scanner and a ration-chit reader are bolted to the same post, badge check third in line. Nobody questions the order anymore.

b: ^Static clocks the scanner's little particulate readout ticking up before you even reach it — another bad-air day nobody's bothering to announce.
^Just routine hardware, as far as you can tell.

root: ^A woman in Aveline colors clears the same post without slowing down — no mask-seal check, just a nod from the guard.

b: ^Graft doesn't need the badge to place her — subdermal ports at the collar, skin that's never once burned under unfiltered sun. Whatever's sealed off past this checkpoint, she's not the kind of modified that queues for anything.
^Just someone who didn't have to wait, as far as you can tell.

root: ^Above the queue, a recruitment screen loops Terra Nova's pitch on a three-second cycle — lunar wage figures scrolling past the mask-seal readouts like just more processing data. EARTH IS HOME. THE FUTURE ISN'T HERE ANYMORE, it finishes, then starts again.

b: ^The Ledger's already subtracting before the loop resets — full board, filtered air, and a transit debt eating that multiple down to something a lot closer to Saigon scale.
^Big numbers. Gone before you can read whatever's printed underneath them.
^You already tried that trick once today. Better not push it twice.
^Try to talk your way to the front.
^The guard shrugs and waves you past the line. Small win.
^He doesn't even look up. "Back of the line."

done: ^Eventually the queue spits you through, badge scanned, no questions asked.
mei_hong_topics: ^Mei Hong gives you her attention again — patient, watchful, still deciding how much this room can afford to say out loud.
^Ask if she's worried about the investigation.
^Ask about the guard at the gate.

c-0: ^"Operations. I keep the lights on and the paperwork honest — most days." She doesn't quite meet your eyes on "honest."
c-1: ^"Corporate optics. Aveline wants to look careful without slowing anyone down who actually matters." A small, tired smile. "You noticed."

b: ^Her composure slips half a second before she catches it. "Worried isn't the word I'd use. Careful, maybe."
^"Worried?" A short laugh, too quick. "I don't have the luxury."

c-3: ^"Him? He's not paid enough to care who's late." She glances toward the checkpoint. "Neither am I, most days."
